description: Opening every valid dataset succeeds (CHECK-1), including datasets with unusual but valid layouts.

cases.description: A committed dataset with no parts.
One part, two row groups of six rows, key pages of two rows; uncompressed PLAIN v1 pages.

Three parts listed out of file-name order, several row groups and pages each, leading/interior/trailing empty row groups, SNAPPY/ZSTD/GZIP, dictionary and DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY keys, data page v1 and v2, sha256 in the manifest, an extension, and a stray Parquet file under the root that is not part of the dataset.

Keys exercising unsigned byte order: NUL, 0x7F/0x80, 0xFF, invalid UTF-8, UTF-8 whose UTF-16 order differs, prefix chains, keys longer than 64 bytes (pyarrow does not shorten bounds), and long keys of 0xFF bytes. Pages of 3 rows.

Projected values of every mandatory physical type with nulls, special floats given by exact bits (signed zero, infinities, NaN payloads), unsigned-annotated INT32/INT64 reported as signed physical values, and a top-level column literally named a.b; the key column carries the STRING annotation; part 1 lacks columns f64 and req, only part 2 has column extra; meta (struct) and tags (list) are nested.

Folder-like keys: keys equal to prefixes, trailing and repeated delimiters, a delimiter at the start, non-ASCII bytes used as delimiters, keys beginning with 0xFF, and the common prefix a/b/ spanning a part boundary. Pages of 2 rows.
Keys a/a, a/z, b/1, b/2, c: the worked example of LIST-7 (bounds apply to candidate keys).
An unannotated key column holding keys that are not valid UTF-8 (allowed, KEY-6). Each invalid key is in the middle of a 3-row page, so every page bound is valid UTF-8.

Columns with logical annotations whose physical values the protocol reports: DATE (INT32 days), TIMESTAMP millis and micros/UTC (INT64), DECIMAL stored as INT32, INT64 and FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY(13) (unscaled two's complement), STRING (BYTE_ARRAY).

Data pages that use the remaining mandatory encodings: part 0 is written as Parquet format 1.0 with dictionaries, so key and value data pages are PLAIN_DICTIONARY; part 1 uses DELTA_BINARY_PACKED for INT32 and INT64 and DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY for BYTE_ARRAY columns (including the key), with data page v2. Asserted from the page headers.

Valid, but two value columns use codecs outside the ENC-1 baseline: lz4col is LZ4_RAW and brcol is BROTLI. The key and size columns are SNAPPY. A reader or validator may support these codecs or report them unsupported.

binary-keys with every key-page bound longer than 16 bytes shortened conservatively (lower bounds to a 16-byte prefix, upper bounds to an incremented prefix, except that an upper bound whose first 16 bytes are all 0xFF is kept full). Adjacent page bounds overlap. Row group 1 of part 0 is marked UNORDERED.

binary-keys with every key-page bound longer than 2 bytes shortened to 2 bytes the same way: e.g. a page ending at ff ff ff keeps its full maximum while its siblings are shortened, and many adjacent bounds overlap.
basic with valid but non-monotone key page bounds (a looser minimum and maximum) and boundary_order UNORDERED.
projection with the key annotated only by the legacy converted type UTF8 (KEY-1 allows it).

basic with an extension holding fractional, exponent, negative, very large, null, boolean, array and nested values, and an escaped surrogate pair: ordinary JSON inside extensions (EXT-1; MAN-6 constrains only the defined integer members).
basic with the ColumnIndex and OffsetIndex of every non-key column removed (allowed: COL-4).
